title: Tenant metadata normalization & index rationalization for control-plane DB
creator: Ava Ortega
description: Refactor control-plane tenant metadata storage to reduce query latency and remove redundant indexes. Current tenant_metadata is a wide jsonb column with multiple ad-hoc indexes that cause bloat and slow writes; this ticket normalizes frequently-accessed fields into a compact relational table, consolidates indexes, and introduces a backfill/migration plan with canary rollout to avoid downtime.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tenant lookup p99 latency for common paths reduced by >=25% under test workload; 2) No increase in steady-state write p95 latency by more than 10%; 3) Migration runs as online backfill with <1% additional error rate; 4) Rollback plan validated in staging and runbook added.
updates: 2025-01-09 - Ava Ortega: Spike completed against staging snapshot. Observed ~35% improvement in SELECT p99 for tenant lookups when removing duplicated jsonb indexes. Trade-off: initial backfill time acceptable (~3 hours for current tenant volume).

2025-01-11 - Liam Chen: Proposed plan submitted: 1) add tenant_metadata_v2 table with columns for tenant_id, org_name, quota_limits, billing_meta; 2) write dual-writes from API behind feature flag; 3) run streaming backfill job that progressively copies existing rows; 4) switch read path; 5) decommission old jsonb columns and indexes. Shared plan in Confluence.

2025-01-13 - PR review (ENG): Reviewed by Priya Rao and Mateo Silva. Priya requested explicit index sizing estimates and to include a throttling parameter for backfill job. Mateo suggested preserving existing partial indexes temporarily to avoid contesting hot path queries during cutover.

2025-01-14 - Performance team: Benchmarked dual-write overhead with canary: write p95 increased by ~6% under synthetic mixed workload; approved within target. Added backfill job CPU cap and adjustable batch size to reduce IO pressure.

2025-01-16 - Liam Chen: Implemented online backfill job with checkpointing. Initial dry-run on pre-prod completed (0 failures). Added metrics: backfill_progress, backfill_error_rate, row_latency_histogram. Dashboards linked in attachments.

2025-01-18 - QA: Ran read-swap canary across 3% of tenants; observed read latency improvements and no data divergence. Found edge-case where legacy tenants with legacy_billing=null caused null-pointer in a join — fixed null handling and added test coverage.

2025-01-20 - Security review: Confirmed no secret material in migration. Access for migration service restricted by role. Security requested audit log entry for schema changes; runbook updated to emit audit events.

2025-01-21 - Liam Chen: Preparing rollout: schedule migration in two waves (non-critical tenants then critical). Rollback strategy: toggle API to read from legacy column, drain backfill, re-create dropped index if needed. Next steps: finalize migration window with SRE and run a full dry-run during maintenance window.

Notes and trade-offs: Normalization adds storage overhead (~12%) due to new table metadata and indexes but reduces per-query work and index bloat. Risk: long-running backfill could contend with OLTP writes—mitigated via throttling and checkpoints. Decision: prioritize read latency for tenant lookups over minimal storage increase.
